newsitem.title: KENYA: Kenya shilling eases marginally on year-end selling.
newsitem.headline: Kenya shilling eases marginally on year-end selling.

text.p: The Kenyan shilling eased marginally on Monday morning on a last minute rush for the dollar from oil importers, commercial bank dealers said.
The Central Bank of Kenya posted a mean shilling average of 55.00 against the dollar from 54.90 on Friday, while on the pound it was posted at 92.93 from 91.93.
Dealers said the oil companies sought to cover every position before the year-end.
"The shilling was also pressured by foreign investors in the Kenyan treasury bill market who were selling their shillings for dollars," one dealer added.
A dealer said the market opened at 55.05 selling and by mid-morning was trading at 55.20.
Some dealers said the increase in demand was temporary and expected the downward pressure on the shilling to ease as trading was still in very thin volumes.
"I expect the rates to go back to normal levels, that is below 55 levels after the January 1," one dealer said.
The money market was tight as a result of corporate tax payments. Overnight rates were quoted at between 18-22 percent from 20 percent on Friday.
